sentences.text:
THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FURTHER HEARING, THIS DAY,
K.S.MUDAGAL J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT "Whether the impugned judgment and order of acquittal passed by the V Additional District &
Sessions Judge, Mysuru, in S.C.No.232/2014 suffers patent illegality or perversity?" is the question involved in this case.
2. Respondent Nos.1 to 3 were accused Nos.1 to 3 in S.C.No.232/2014 before the trial Court.

They were tried in the said case for the charges for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 304B read with 34 of IPC and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 (for short, 'DP' Act), on the basis of the charge sheet filed in Crime No.163/2013 by Badanavalu Police station, Nanjangud Taluk, Mysuru District.
For the purpose of convenience, the parties are referred to henceforth according to their ranks before the trial Court.

The respondents were charge sheeted in Crime No.163/2013 on the basis of the complaint filed by PW-1, the father of deceased Lakshmi, as per Ex.P-4.
4.

Some admitted facts of the case are as follows:
i) PWs-1 & 9 are brothers. PWs-1 & 2 are the father and mother, PWs-3 & 4 are the brothers of deceased Lakshmi. PW-9 is the father, PW-22 is the mother, PW-23 is the brother of deceased Jayalakshmi.
ii) On 21.08.2013 at 03.00 p.m. Lakshmi & Jayalakshmi drowned in the right bank channel of Kabini river near Kirugunda village.
The dead bodies were traced in the said channel on the next day.

5. The case of the prosecution is as follows:
State Of Karnataka vs Girisha @ Giriraju on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77077430/
2

entities.text: State Of Karnataka vs Girisha @ Giriraju
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accused Nos.2 & 3 are the parents of accused No.1.
Accused No.1 was married to Lakshmi on 01.07.2013 and the same was subsequently registered.
That was a love marriage.

Within few days of the marriage, accused Nos.1 to 3 sent back Lakshmi demanding that she shall bring 30 grams of gold and 1 NC: 2024:KHC:21210-DB motorcycle from her family as she has not brought any dowry at the time of marriage.
At the intervention of PWs-15, 16 and 18, the village elders, the panchayat was held between the parents of the victim and the accused.
The parents of the victim sought one month's time to pay the dowry articles demanded.

On 16.08.2013, the accused after assaulting the victim drove her out of their house on the ground that she did not bring the demanded articles even after the lapse of one month and she has entered the house eloping with accused No.1 and she has no place in their house.

Therefore,
she was staying in her parents house.
On 21.08.2013 at 11.30 a.m. she went to the house of accused pleading them to allow her in their house.
Accused again demanded the dowry, harassed her and drove her out.
Being unable to withstand the same, on the same day at 03.00p.m. she committed suicide by jumping into the right bank channel of Kabini river near Kirugunda village.
Her cousin Jayalakshmi went to the rescue of Lakshmi and she also accidentally fell into the channel and died.

On the complaint of PW-1 in that regard, the FIR as per Ex.P-31 was registered against the accused and after investigation charge sheet was filed.
NC: 2024:KHC:21210-DB 6.
The trial Court, on hearing both side, framed the charges against the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 304B read with Section 34 of IPC and Section 4 of DP Act.
Since accused denied the charges, trial was conducted.
In support of the case of prosecution PWs-1 to 33 were examined and Exs.P-1 to P-31 were marked and MOs.1 to 7 were marked.
The accused, after their examination under Section 313 of Cr.P.C., did not lead any defence evidence.
7. The trial Court, on hearing the parties, by the impugned judgment and order, acquitted the accused holding that the charges against the accused were not proved beyond reasonable doubt.
The State has preferred the above appeal challenging the said judgment and order of acquittal.
8. Sri.
Rajath Subramanaya, learned High Court Government Pleader reiterating the grounds of appeal, submits that the victim died within two months of the marriage and death of Lakshmi was unnatural one.

He further submits that the evidence of PWs-1 to 4 shows that the victim was subjected to cruelty in connection with demand for dowry, therefore, presumption under Section 113A of the Indian Evidence Act, NC: 2024:KHC:21210-DB 1872 ('Evidence Act' for short) arises.
The accused did not rebut the said presumption.
The trial Court failed to take note of the same.
Therefore, the impugned judgment and order of acquittal is unsustainable in law.

9. Per contra, Sri.N.S.Sampangi Ramaiah, learned amicus-curiae submits that this being an appeal against the judgment and order of acquittal, same cannot be interfered with unless the same is shown to be patently illegal or perverse.
Except PWs-1 to 4, who are the interested witnesses, none of the witnesses supported the theory of demand of dowry or the death being suicidal one.

The State Of Karnataka vs Girisha @ Giriraju on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77077430/
3 evidence on record sufficiently shows that deaths were accidental one.

entities.text: State Of Karnataka vs Girisha @ Giriraju
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the absence of harassment in connection with the demand for dowry, the presumption under Section 113A of the Evidence Act is not available.

He submits that in the instant case, the daughter of PWs-9 & 22 had also died, they themselves did not support the theory of PWs-1 to 4. PWs-15, 16 & 18, the alleged witnesses for demand of the accused and negotiation to gain time, did not support the prosecution version.
Therefore, evidence of PWs-1 to 4 was rightly disbelieved by the trial Court.
The trial Court's judgment is based on sound NC: 2024:KHC:21210-DB appreciation of evidence on record.
The appeal deserves no merit and is liable to be dismissed.
Analysis 10.
As noted above, there is no dispute that the victim was married to accused No.1 on 01.07.2013 and she died on 21.08.2013 by drowning.
Along with her, her cousin sister Jayalakshmi also drowned in the same channel.
According to the prosecution, Lakshmi committed suicide by jumping into channel water and when Jayalakshmi went to her rescue, she also drowned accidentally and died.
The accused denied any dowry harassment and their defence was that both Lakshmi and Jayalakshmi fell into the channel accidentally and died.
The burden was on the prosecution to prove that soon before her death, Lakshmi was subjected to ill-treatment in connection with the demand for dowry.
Secondly, prosecution had to prove that the death of Lakshmi was suicidal one.
11. It is the settled proposition of law that the scope of interference in an appeal against the judgment and order of acquittal is limited.

Unless it is shown that impugned judgment and order of acquittal suffers patent illegality and perversity, NC: 2024:KHC:21210-DB the appellate Court cannot interfere with the same merely because a second view is possible.

In such cases at the appellate stage, the accused have double benefit, the first one being the presumption of innocence at the trial stage, secondly which gets reinforced by the judgment and order of acquittal.
This view of ours is supported by the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Prem Singh vs. State of Haryana1.

entities.text: Prem Singh vs. State of Haryana1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the light of the said judgment, this Court has to see whether the trial Court committed patent illegality or perversity in rejecting the evidence of the prosecution regarding the dowry harassment and death being suicidal one.

12. Admittedly, accused No.1 and deceased Lakshmi had a romantic relationship even before their marriage and they had eloped, in that regard, PW-1 had filed report as per Ex.P-1 before Badanavalu police station alleging that his daughter Lakshmi has eloped with accused No.1 and before he filing the complaint, they have come together to Badanavalu police station.

In the complaint he further stated that since she is aged below 18 years, he would like to take her back to his (2013) 14 SCC 88 NC: 2024:KHC:21210-DB house and he may be permitted for the same and accused shall be warned not to talk to the victim.

The evidence of PW-1, the father of Lakshmi, as well as PW-28, the then Head Constable of Badanavalu police station shows that by the time PW-1 gave the complaint to their police station, both accused No.1 and Lakshmi appeared in the police station and reported that they were loving each other and as the parents of Lakshmi did not accept their relationship, they had gone to the house of sister of accused No.1.
After counseling, the parents of both parties agreed for performing the marriage after Lakshmi attaining majority.
On recording the statements of concerned, the victim was sent back with PW-1.

4 13.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also the admitted fact that later the marriage of accused No.1 and Lakshmi was performed on 01.07.2013 in Kirugunda village and the marriage expenses were borne by accused Nos.2 & 3.

According to PWs-1 to 4, after the marriage, the victim was subjected to cruelty demanding 30 grams of gold and one motorcycle on the ground that no dowry was given at the time of marriage and in that regard panchayat was convened and in that panchayat at the intervention of PWs-15, 16 & 18, one month's time was fixed for giving - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:21210-DB motorcycle and gold.

Though PWs-1 to 4 reiterated the said contention,
PWs-15, 16 & 18, who allegedly acted as mediators in the matter, did not support the prosecution version.
As against that they denied that they have given statement before the police.
PWs-1 to 4 being relatives of the victim, it would be unsafe to rely on their evidence without any corroboration.
As aforesaid, PWs-15, 16 & 18 did not support the allegation of demand of dowry or cruelty in connection with demand of dowry.
14. PWs-9, 22 & 23 were the close relatives of PWs-1 to 4 and the victim.
They are none-else but the parents and brother of the other victim Jayalakshmi.
If there was any domestic violence in connection with any demand of dowry or even otherwise that would have been within their knowledge being the close relatives.
But they did not support the prosecution version or the version of PWs-1 to 4 regarding the demand of dowry or ill-treatment in connection with such demand of dowry.
They did not even support the theory of commission of suicide by Lakshmi.
They say that they came to know that when their daughter went to the rescue of Lakshmi, when she was drowning in the channel water, she also drowned - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:21210-DB and died.
They denied having given statement before the IO imputing cruelty to the accused in connection with demand for dowry or Lakshmi committing suicide.
15. To prove that the death of Lakshmi was suicidal one, the prosecution relied on the evidence of PW-10, the only eye-witness to suicidal death.

According to the prosecution on 21.08.2013 at 03.00 p.m., PW-10 was riding his bicycle near the scene of offence and he found Lakshmi crying and moving towards the nala followed by Jayalakshmi and suddenly Lakshmi jumping into the water and when Jayalakshmi went to her rescue, she also fell into the channel and he has given the statement to that effect.
But he totally turned hostile to the prosecution and denied having given such statement before the IO.

16. Though the Public Prosecutor cross-examined PWs- 15, 16, 18, 9, 22 & 23 on treating them hostile, nothing worth was elicited in their cross-examination to demonstrate that they were in any way interested in the accused, therefore, they have deliberately turned hostile.

Under such circumstances, the trial Court was justified in holding that the allegations of cruelty - 12 - State Of Karnataka vs Girisha @ Giriraju on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77077430/
5 NC: 2024:KHC:21210-DB in connection with demand for dowry and death being suicidal one was not proved.

entities.text: State Of Karnataka vs Girisha @ Giriraju
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 17. To invoke the presumption under Section 113A of the Evidence Act, the death being unnatural and was within seven years of marriage alone are not sufficient.
To raise such presumption the prosecution is required to prove that soon before her death, the victim was subjected to cruelty by her husband or his relatives in connection with demand for dowry.

Only on proving the said aspect,
presumption arises and the burden shifts on the accused to rebut the said presumption.
In the present case, the initial burden of proving demand for dowry and ill-treatment in connection with demand for dowry themselves were not proved.
Therefore, the submission that Section 113A of the Evidence Act arises and that was not considered by the trial Court deserves no merit.
18. Looked from any angle, impugned judgment and order of acquittal does not suffer any patent illegality or perversity warranting the interference of this Court.
Hence, the appeal is liable to be dismissed.

Hence the following:
- 13 - NC: 2024:KHC:21210-DB ORDER
The appeal is dismissed.
Court places on record its appreciation for the able assistance rendered by Sri.N.S.Sampangi Ramaiah, learned Amicus-Curiae.
Registry shall disburse him remuneration of Rs.15,000/- forthwith.
